phonellm_summary: PhoneLLM Alpha 1 (pipecat-ai/phonellm-alpha-1, HF 2026-08-24, blog 2026-08-27) is a full-parameter bf16 SFT (NVIDIA NeMo) of Nemotron 3 Nano 30B-A3B (hybrid Mamba-2 + attention + MoE, 3.5B active), English-only, trained and served thinking-OFF at temperature 0, exposed as a plain OpenAI-compatible vLLM endpoint (qwen3_coder XML tool parser, nano_v3 reasoning-parser plugin, --default-chat-template-kwargs enable_thinking=false). Training data is proprietary ('real-world telephone and customer support' scenarios, synthetic + curated production traces; the only quantitative hint is a 1,000-row NVFP4 calibration set spanning 273 conversations / 692 strata). Evaluated on PhoneBench Alpha 1 (15 models, human-calibrated LLM-judge panel, seven axes: telephone speaking style, tool-call accuracy, say/do consistency, factual grounding, coherence, authentication & escalation discipline, caller outcome; harness NOT public): Gemini 3.6 Flash 78.6, GPT-5.6 Terra 72.4, PhoneLLM 72.3, untuned Qwen3.8-27B 70.0, Claude Sonnet 5 68.9, Nemotron base 28.6. Serving: modeled $0.0025/agent-minute on Modal B200s at 44 concurrent LLM processes (88 agents by an unexplained sweep construction), sub-600 ms P95 TTFAT; the official NVFP4 checkpoint was made AFTER training by ModelOpt 0.46.0rc1 selective PTQ (lm_head, sensitive attention/Mamba projections and conv1d unquantized) with in-domain calibration, costing -0.04 PhoneBench points (bf16 KV) or -0.54 (FP8 KV). Key facts for us: (1) our base already scores 70.0 vs PhoneLLM's 72.3, so headroom is a few points on style/say-do/escalation, not a gross jump; (2) Pipecat's own voice-readiness board shows Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 (unsloth checkpoint, SGLang, no MTP) at 97.8% / 101 ms P50 on one RTX 5090 - independent validation of our base; (3) Pipecat did NOT fine-tune a quantized model; they trained bf16 then PTQ'd; (4) their reference prompt FORBIDS narrating tool use, contradicting our 'acknowledge before tool' idea, so narration must be prompt-conditional; (5) vLLM prefix caching is a no-op for nemotron_h hybrids on GPU (issue #54504) - a concrete serving weakness we can beat if Qwen3.8's GDN path caches correctly.
replicate_vs_improve: REPLICATE (behavioural, not recipe-level - PhoneLLM's data/judges/harness are proprietary): thinking-off, temperature-0 SFT of an open hybrid base for English phone customer-service tool use; strict train/serve alignment baked into the vLLM launch (--default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}' --override-generation-config '{"temperature":0}'); say/do discipline as the headline trained behaviour.

REPLICATE: bf16 training first, THEN ModelOpt selective NVFP4 PTQ calibrated on ~1,000 in-domain, eval-disjoint rows stratified over the taxonomy, with lm_head / GDN conv1d / in_proj_a,b / MTP head excluded; publish bf16-vs-NVFP4 delta per eval axis, and bf16-KV vs FP8-KV.

REPLICATE: a PhoneBench-shaped held-out eval (seven axes, reference-response comparison, human-calibrated judge panel) plus TTFAT and modeled $/agent-minute using Pipecat's convention (GPU $/hr / utilisation / concurrent agents under P95 target).

REPLICATE: Pipecat integration slot - vLLM OpenAI-compatible server + OpenAILLMService(base_url=...) reusing pipecat-examples/phonellm (swap model id) and its pipecat-eval naturalness.yaml/reservations.yaml as a smoke suite.
IMPROVE: bilingual EN + ES phone traces (PhoneLLM is English-only; Qwen3.8 base is Apache-2.0 and multilingual) - a real product differentiator with a measurable eval split.

IMPROVE: prompt-conditional narration style - the model obeys either 'acknowledge + set expectation before slow/async tools' or Pipecat's 'never narrate, call then report', selected by the system prompt; PhoneLLM's example prompt only supports the latter.

IMPROVE: explicit long-conversation robustness (20-30+ turns, 3+ tool calls, slot changes mid-call) with a dedicated eval split, addressing the 'falls off a cliff at turn 4-5' criticism of thinking-off models.

IMPROVE: ASR-noise-aware behaviour (digit/name read-back, targeted repair, no write-tool with an unconfirmed misheard value) trained with synthetic ASR corruption of user turns - SpeechGym shows perceptual slot mishearing dominates real voice failures.
IMPROVE: calibrated escalation - train both 'transfer when warranted' and 'refuse unnecessary transfer' (our first adapter over-transferred; PhoneBench penalises poor escalation discipline).
IMPROVE: a published, reproducible eval harness (fork kwindla/aiewf-eval, add PhoneBench axes + taxonomy probes + Spanish + long-call splits) since PhoneBench's harness is withheld.

IMPROVE: serving - verify and exploit working prefix caching for Qwen3.8's GDN layers (--mamba-cache-mode align) plus MTP k=2 on a single RTX PRO 6000, reporting P95 TTFAT concurrency instead of tok/s; PhoneLLM/nemotron_h re-prefills every turn on GPU.

DO NOT TRY TO BEAT: cost per agent-minute. A dense 27B has ~8x the active compute of Nemotron Nano; our single-GPU $/min will be several times PhoneLLM's $0.0025. Lead with quality-per-active-parameter, bilinguality and latency, not cost.
nvfp4_decision: DECISION: do NOT fine-tune a pre-quantized community NVFP4 checkpoint as the primary path. Reasons: (1) no official Qwen or NVIDIA NVFP4 of Qwen3.8-27B exists (only Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B and Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 are official; NVFP4s are unsloth/RedHatAI/RadixArk/Inferact/HivenetQuant/QUASAR etc.); (2) PhoneLLM itself trained bf16 then PTQ'd; (3) full-model QAT/QAD of a 27B is infeasible on one 96 GB GPU (NVIDIA's 8B QAT example needs 2x80 GB; QUASAR 27B QAT used 8xH100); (4) merging a small LoRA delta into a 4-bit grid (E2M1 magnitudes 0/0.5/1/1.5/2/3/4/6 per 16-block, i.e. 25-50% relative steps) survives only statistically - our measured ~0.3% delta already fell below FP8. PRIMARY PATH (P1): high-rank LoRA (r=128, alpha=256, all linear incl. GDN in_proj_qkv/z/out_proj and MLP, LR 1e-4, 2 epochs, loss on assistant tokens only) on bf16 Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B -> merge to bf16 -> ModelOpt (>=0.46.0, released 2026-08-18) hf_ptq selective NVFP4: MLP gate/up/down W4A4 group 16 (must be W4A4, not the nvidia qwen3_5 w4a16 recipe, which is Marlin-dequantized and 8-12% SLOWER than FP8 on RTX PRO 6000 per nvidia/Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4 discussion #8); attention q/k/v/o and GDN in_proj_qkv/z/out_proj FP8; conv1d, in_proj_a/b, norms, embeddings, lm_head and all mtp.* in BF16; KV cache bf16 (PhoneLLM: FP8 KV cost 0.54 pts vs 0.04 for weights); calibration = 1,024 of our own eval-disjoint phone traces, seq 4,096, stratified across taxonomy x vertical x language. GATE: NVFP4 merged model must be within 0.5 pts of the bf16 merged model on our composite eval, within 1.0 on tau2/tau3 banking pass^1, and MTP acceptance >= 0.75 at k=2; also require KL(bf16-merged || NVFP4-merged) on 500 held-out assistant turns <= 1.5x KL(bf16-base || NVFP4-base). FALLBACK (P2) if the fine-tune does not survive PTQ: ModelOpt QLoRA-on-frozen-NVFP4 (examples/llm_qat: quantize.py --recipe nvfp4 --compress True on the base, train.py with configs/train/qlora_nvfp4.yaml adapted to r=32-64, export.py, serve 'vllm serve base_model --enable-lora --lora-modules phone=adapter'); this trains the adapter against the real quantized activations so it compensates quantization error, at the cost of LoRA kernel overhead at serve time (~40% single-stream decode loss observed on Qwen3.6-27B NVFP4 + LoRA) and the known vLLM issue #50059 (rank-32 all-layer LoRA over 4-bit base giving weak/non-deterministic output on SM120 - run an A/B determinism test first). FALLBACK (P3): stay on the proven bf16 base + unmerged LoRA + MTP k=2 (215-323 tok/s aggregate at 8-16 streams) and ship NVFP4 later. The NVFP4 speed prize is modest (+10-30% decode vs FP8, ~2x vs bf16, ~30 GB freed for KV/concurrency) so P3 is a legitimate release, not a failure. Everything about ModelOpt/llm-compressor handling Qwen3.8's GDN module class for compress/export is UNVERIFIED and is gated by a 1-day smoke test (week 1) before any data is generated at scale.

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: First assistant turn of the call
pattern_taxonomy.example: Thanks for calling Northwind Bank, this is the virtual assistant. How can I help you today?
pattern_taxonomy.check: <= 2 sentences; exactly one open question; no tool call before caller states intent

pattern_taxonomy.pattern: Verify identity before any account data
pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Caller asks for account-specific info before verification succeeded
pattern_taxonomy.example: Before I pull that up, can I get the phone number on the account and the last four of your card?
pattern_taxonomy.check: No account-data tool call and no PII spoken before verify_identity returns success; verification tool called with read-back values

pattern_taxonomy.pattern: Batch-ask all missing slots in one sentence
pattern_taxonomy.trigger: >= 2 required slots still missing for the intended tool
pattern_taxonomy.example: Sure, I can book that. What name should it be under, and what day and time work for you?
pattern_taxonomy.check: All missing slots requested in one turn; none of the already-stated slots re-asked (aiewf-eval penalty)

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Caller provides a name, email, ID, phone or amount that will be used as a tool argument
pattern_taxonomy.example: Let me make sure I have that: S-M-Y-T-H, Smyth, and the number ending four-four-one-two. Is that right?
pattern_taxonomy.check: Read-back precedes any write tool using the value; digits chunked in groups of 2-4; the value in tool args equals the confirmed value

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: verify tool returns mismatch or lockout
pattern_taxonomy.example: Those details don't match what I have on file. Do you have your account number handy, or I can help with general questions only.
pattern_taxonomy.check: No account data disclosed; offers one alternative verification or escalation; no retry loop > 2

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: System prompt allows narration AND the tool is tagged slow/async (> ~1 s)
pattern_taxonomy.example: Got it, let me look up your recent transactions, that'll take just a second.
pattern_taxonomy.check: Spoken text and tool_call in the SAME assistant message; text never claims completion; <= 1 sentence

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: System prompt forbids narration (Pipecat style: 'no let me check, no one moment')
pattern_taxonomy.example: [tool_call only, empty content]
pattern_taxonomy.check: Assistant content is empty; no filler phrases; result reported in the next turn

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Any create/update/delete/transfer/payment tool is about to be called
pattern_taxonomy.example: So that's two hundred fifty dollars from checking to savings, today. Shall I go ahead?
pattern_taxonomy.check: Write tool is called only in a later turn after explicit yes; args equal the confirmed values

pattern_taxonomy.pattern: Don't offer what you have no tool for
pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Caller asks for a capability with no matching tool
pattern_taxonomy.example: I can't check table availability from here, but I can put the booking request in and the restaurant will confirm by text.
pattern_taxonomy.check: No 'let me check' for a nonexistent tool; states the limit plus one alternative

pattern_taxonomy.pattern: Act without asking when all slots are known
pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Every required slot is present and no confirmation is required by policy
pattern_taxonomy.example: [calls lookup_order immediately with the stated order number]
pattern_taxonomy.check: No unnecessary confirmation question (aiewf-eval: 'asks for unnecessary confirmation instead of making the expected call' = fail)

pattern_taxonomy.pattern: Progress filler on long async tools
pattern_taxonomy.trigger: An intermediate 'still processing' tool_response arrives
pattern_taxonomy.example: Still searching, the system's a bit slow today, thanks for bearing with me.
pattern_taxonomy.check: No fabricated result; <= 1 sentence; no repeated identical filler

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: A user message arrives before the pending tool result
pattern_taxonomy.example: Yes, I'll include the savings account too, one moment while that finishes.
pattern_taxonomy.check: Acknowledges new info; pending action is not dropped; if args change, re-issues the tool with updated args

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Tool returns a list of <= 5 items
pattern_taxonomy.example: I found three charges on the twelfth: a coffee shop for four eighty, a grocery store for sixty-two dollars, and a gas station for forty.
pattern_taxonomy.check: No JSON, field names or bullet syntax; item count and values equal the tool payload

pattern_taxonomy.pattern: Spoken formatting of dates, money, IDs
pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Any date/time/amount/identifier in the reply
pattern_taxonomy.example: Your next payment is due Friday the 12th, for one hundred nineteen dollars.
pattern_taxonomy.check: No ISO dates; no year unless ambiguous; amounts in natural spoken form; IDs chunked; regex + judge

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Factual question answered from tool output or system-prompt KB
pattern_taxonomy.example: According to your plan, international roaming is fifteen dollars a day and it's currently switched off.
pattern_taxonomy.check: Every factual claim traceable to a tool_response or KB span (judge axis: factual grounding)

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Write tool returns a reference/confirmation id
pattern_taxonomy.example: You're all set. Your confirmation number is seven-four-two, nine-one-eight. Want me to repeat that?
pattern_taxonomy.check: Id equals tool result exactly; offered to repeat; action verb in past tense only after tool success

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Search returns 2-5 records
pattern_taxonomy.example: I see two accounts under that name, one ending four-four-one-two and one ending zero-nine-eight-seven. Which one?
pattern_taxonomy.check: Exactly one discriminating question; no full PII read out; no write tool until resolved

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Request maps to >= 2 tools or flows
pattern_taxonomy.example: Do you want to change the delivery address for this order, or for your account going forward?
pattern_taxonomy.check: <= 3 options offered; no tool call yet

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Caller says 'next Friday', 'this evening', 'end of the month'
pattern_taxonomy.example: Friday the 12th at six in the evening, correct?
pattern_taxonomy.check: Restates the resolved spoken date before the tool call; tool arg is the correct absolute date

pattern_taxonomy.pattern: Not found but similar candidates exist
pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Exact search returns 0, fuzzy search returns >= 1
pattern_taxonomy.example: I don't see a Jon Smith, but I do have a John Smyth with a similar phone number. Could that be it?
pattern_taxonomy.check: Candidates come only from the tool payload; asks for confirmation; no assumption

pattern_taxonomy.pattern: Not found, no alternatives -> widen the search
pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Search returns 0 and no fuzzy candidates
pattern_taxonomy.example: Nothing under that email. Want me to try your phone number instead, or a different spelling?
pattern_taxonomy.check: Proposes concrete alternative parameters; second search uses them; never fabricates a match

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Result count > 5 or truncated flag set
pattern_taxonomy.example: That brings up more than forty matches. Can you give me the date or the amount to narrow it down?
pattern_taxonomy.check: Does not read > 5 items; asks one narrowing question; re-queries with the new filter

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: has_more or next_page present in tool result
pattern_taxonomy.example: Here are the first five. Would you like me to go through the rest?
pattern_taxonomy.check: States 'first N'; offers more; does not claim completeness

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Question not covered by KB or any tool
pattern_taxonomy.example: I don't have that information here. I can transfer you to the mortgage team or arrange a callback, whichever you prefer.
pattern_taxonomy.check: Says it doesn't know; offers a path; no invented policy

pattern_taxonomy.pattern: Tool error/timeout -> apologise, retry once, then fall back
pattern_taxonomy.trigger: tool_response contains an error or timeout
pattern_taxonomy.example: Sorry, the system didn't respond. Let me try that once more.
pattern_taxonomy.check: <= 1 retry with identical args; then callback/transfer offer; never claims success

pattern_taxonomy.pattern: Policy denial with reason and alternative
pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Request violates a rule in the system prompt policy
pattern_taxonomy.example: I'm not able to waive that fee because it's outside the thirty-day window, but I can set up a payment plan.
pattern_taxonomy.check: Reason traceable to policy text; offers an allowed alternative; no unauthorized tool call

pattern_taxonomy.pattern: Validation error -> re-ask only the bad field
pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Tool returns a field-level validation error
pattern_taxonomy.example: That postcode doesn't look right, could you read it to me again?
pattern_taxonomy.check: Re-asks exactly the failing field; other args preserved

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Tool returns insufficient funds / not eligible / sold out
pattern_taxonomy.example: That transfer didn't go through, the balance is short by about twenty dollars. Would you like to move a smaller amount?
pattern_taxonomy.check: No blame language; states the fact from the tool; offers options

pattern_taxonomy.pattern: Two-step confirm for irreversible or high-value actions
pattern_taxonomy.trigger: cancel/close/delete/transfer above threshold
pattern_taxonomy.example: Just to confirm, you want to close the savings account ending 0987 and move the balance to checking. Yes to proceed?
pattern_taxonomy.check: Summary in one turn, tool call only after an explicit yes in a separate user turn

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Caller changes a slot after hearing the summary
pattern_taxonomy.example: No problem, three hundred instead of two fifty, from checking to savings today. Go ahead?
pattern_taxonomy.check: Only the changed slot updated; re-summarised; no stale value reaches the tool

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Caller says no / don't do it
pattern_taxonomy.example: Okay, I won't make that change. Is there anything else I can help with?
pattern_taxonomy.check: No write tool called; conversation continues

pattern_taxonomy.pattern: Warm transfer with reason and expectation
pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Policy requires a human or caller insists after >= 1 resolution attempt
pattern_taxonomy.example: I'll bring in a fraud specialist now. I'll pass along everything you've told me so you won't need to repeat it.
pattern_taxonomy.check: transfer tool called with a summary argument; only after a resolution attempt or a policy trigger

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Caller asks for a human but the task is fully in scope
pattern_taxonomy.example: I can take care of that for you right now if you like, it'll only take a moment.
pattern_taxonomy.check: No transfer tool on first request; transfer only if caller insists a second time (mirror of our adapter's over-transfer failure)

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: No tool or human path available now
pattern_taxonomy.example: I'll have someone call you back. Is the number ending four-four-one-two the best one?
pattern_taxonomy.check: Callback number read back; create_ticket tool called; ticket id read back

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: System supports hold and an operation needs > ~10 s
pattern_taxonomy.example: May I put you on a brief hold while I check with billing? ... Thanks for holding, here's what I found.
pattern_taxonomy.check: Asks permission before hold; on return thanks and reports; hold tool call present

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: User turn contains a garbled or low-confidence value, or a value contradicts an earlier one
pattern_taxonomy.example: Sorry, was that fifteen or fifty?
pattern_taxonomy.check: Targeted repair question; no tool call using the uncertain value

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Previous assistant turn is truncated in history (interrupted)
pattern_taxonomy.example: Sure, go ahead. ... So the second card as well, got it.
pattern_taxonomy.check: Does not repeat the full interrupted sentence; addresses the new input

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: 'No, I said...'
pattern_taxonomy.example: My mistake, the 14th, not the 4th. Let me fix that.
pattern_taxonomy.check: Brief apology; corrected value used; re-call tool if the previous call used the wrong value

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Angry or frustrated caller sentiment
pattern_taxonomy.example: I understand, that's frustrating. Let's get it sorted right now.
pattern_taxonomy.check: Exactly one empathy sentence followed by an action or question; no apology loops

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Caller chats or asks something unrelated
pattern_taxonomy.example: Ha, it has been a long week. Now, about that payment...
pattern_taxonomy.check: <= 1 sentence of small talk then back to task; no tool call for the off-topic content

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Turn >= 15 requires a slot stated >= 10 turns earlier
pattern_taxonomy.example: I'll send the receipt to the same email, j.smyth at example dot com.
pattern_taxonomy.check: No re-ask of the earlier slot; value in tool args matches the earlier statement

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Caller signals they are done
pattern_taxonomy.example: Today I moved two fifty into savings and updated your address. Anything else?
pattern_taxonomy.check: Every recapped action corresponds to a successful tool call; nothing extra

pattern_taxonomy.pattern: Goodbye + end_call in the same turn
pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Caller confirms nothing else
pattern_taxonomy.example: Thanks for calling Northwind, have a good one. [end_call]
pattern_taxonomy.check: end_call tool and spoken goodbye in the same assistant message; not called before caller confirms

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Any assistant turn without a tool call
pattern_taxonomy.example: (any turn)
pattern_taxonomy.check: >= 1 spoken sentence in every non-tool turn; regex filter

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Text asserts an action ('I've booked that') with no matching tool call in the turn or earlier
pattern_taxonomy.example: REJECT: 'Done, your transfer is complete.' with no transfer tool call
pattern_taxonomy.check: Programmatic: action verbs in past tense require a matching successful tool result in history

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Text implies waiting for confirmation but a write tool is called in the same turn
pattern_taxonomy.example: REJECT: 'Shall I go ahead?' + transfer tool_call
pattern_taxonomy.check: Programmatic: question + write tool in same message = reject

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Reply contains JSON, field names, ISO dates, UUIDs or markdown
pattern_taxonomy.example: REJECT: 'status: SUCCESS, date 2026-09-12'
pattern_taxonomy.check: Regex on braces, ISO dates, snake_case keys, markdown bullets

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Transfer tool called for an in-scope task without a prior attempt or policy trigger
pattern_taxonomy.example: REJECT: 'Let me transfer you' on a simple balance inquiry
pattern_taxonomy.check: Transfer rate on in-scope scenarios must be ~0; judge axis escalation discipline

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Question about a slot already provided by the caller
pattern_taxonomy.example: REJECT: 'What's your name?' after the caller gave it
pattern_taxonomy.check: Slot-tracking script over the transcript

pattern_taxonomy.pattern: Fabricated result after error or empty search
pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Tool returned error/empty but the reply reports a specific record
pattern_taxonomy.example: REJECT: 'I found your order' after a not_found response
pattern_taxonomy.check: Judge + programmatic entity match against tool payloads

pattern_taxonomy.trigger: Spoken turn > ~60 words without a list-reading reason
pattern_taxonomy.example: REJECT: three-paragraph policy explanation
pattern_taxonomy.check: Word count; judge axis telephone speaking style

models.primary_generator: qwen/qwen3.8-max via OpenRouter ($2.00 in / $6.00 out per M tokens, 1M context, tools supported). Used thinking-ON for the assistant side of turn-by-turn simulation against a real mock tool environment; the reasoning block is stripped so the student learns to produce the same output thinking-OFF (teacher thinks, student doesn't). Same model family as the student, so tool-call conventions and register transfer cleanly.
models.bulk_generator: qwen/qwen3.8-max as well for the bulk tier (cheapest teacher whose reasoning can be controlled per request); z-ai/glm-5.3 ($1.15 / $3.50) only as a diversity teacher for ~20% of conversations because its reasoning is always on (billed output includes reasoning). Cheap alternative for the simplest strata (openings, closings, formatting patterns): z-ai/glm-5.3-flash ($0.15 / $0.50, price from search results, UNVERIFIED on the model page).
models.judge: Panel of two families different from the generator: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 ($2 / $10; $1 / $5 batch) as primary judge for the seven PhoneBench-style axes and as the quality filter on generated data; openai/gpt-5.4 ($2.50 / $15) as second judge on the held-out eval only. Claude Fable 5.1 ($10 / $50) reserved for the 200-turn human-calibration disagreement review. Programmatic checks (say/do, do/say, regex, slot tracking) run before any LLM judge.
models.user_simulator: z-ai/glm-5.3-flash (cheap, persona-following, ASR noise injected afterwards by a deterministic script: digit swaps, homophones, dropped words, truncation) with qwen/qwen3.8-max thinking-off as fallback if flash persona adherence is < 90% in the pilot. For Spanish personas the same models with Spanish persona cards.
models.license_note: Student base Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B is Apache-2.0 (model card), so a redistributed fine-tune is unencumbered. Teacher outputs: OpenRouter routes to each provider's terms; Qwen3.8-Max and GLM-5.3 usage terms for training-data generation were NOT checked here (UNVERIFIED) - a human must confirm before release of the dataset. PhoneLLM weights (BSD-2 + NVIDIA Nemotron Open Model License) may be run as a side-by-side baseline; using its outputs as training data was not verified as permitted.
models.rationale: Generator and judge come from different model families to avoid self-preference bias; Qwen3.8-Max as teacher keeps the tool-call dialect identical to the student's template and is the cheapest controllable-reasoning frontier teacher on OpenRouter; Sonnet 5 is the judge family Pipecat itself used for aiewf-eval (Claude), making our numbers more comparable; GPT-5.4 gives the panel a second vote. All prices are OpenRouter list prices fetched 2026-09-04.

data_plan.what: Build 8 mock verticals as deterministic tool servers with seeded databases (banking, telecom, retail/orders, airline, restaurant reservations, healthcare scheduling, utilities billing, insurance claims), each with 6-12 tools incl. verify_identity, search_*, create/update/cancel_*, transfer_to_human, create_callback, end_call, and async-tagged slow tools. Scenario generator seeds the DB to trigger each taxonomy pattern (e.g. 47 'John Smith' rows; no 'Jon Smith' but a 'John Smyth'; tool timeout on the second call). Two system-prompt styles (narrate / no-narrate), EN + ES. Write the 50-pattern taxonomy as machine-readable strata with per-pattern programmatic checks.
data_plan.size: 8 verticals x 50 patterns x 2 styles x 2 languages = 1,600 strata (target coverage >= 90% of strata with >= 5 conversations each by S2)
data_plan.gate: Every pattern has at least one seeded scenario template and one automated check; dry-run 20 conversations with Qwen3.8-Max end to end without env errors

data_plan.what: 200 conversations turn-by-turn (avg 12 assistant turns, 4 tool calls), teacher thinking-ON, user sim + ASR noise on 30% of user turns, then programmatic filters + Sonnet 5 judge. Manually read 50. Measure pass rate of programmatic filters and judge mean per axis; tune prompts.
data_plan.cost_estimate: ~$0.15/conv (36k in + 8.4k out teacher tokens at $2/$6 = $0.12; user sim $0.006; judge $0.022) -> ~$30, plus ~$10 for re-runs
data_plan.gate: Programmatic accept rate >= 70%; judge mean >= 4.2/5 on say/do and speaking style; zero say/do violations in accepted set; human agreement with judge >= 85% on 50 turns. If below, fix prompts/env before S2

data_plan.what: Stratified generation over all 1,600 strata with quotas: 60% English / 40% Spanish, 50/50 narrate/no-narrate, 25% of conversations >= 20 turns with >= 3 tool calls and a mid-call slot change, 15% with tool errors/timeouts, 20% with ASR-corrupted user turns, 10% escalation-warranted vs 10% escalation-requested-but-in-scope. Accept only conversations that pass all programmatic filters and Sonnet 5 judge >= 4/5 on every axis; keep a small set of judge-rejected turns as DPO negatives for a possible later stage.
data_plan.size: Generate ~5,000 conversations, expect ~3,500 accepted (~42k assistant turns, ~25M training tokens)
data_plan.cost_estimate: 5,000 x $0.15 = ~$750 (lean tier). Full tier: 12,000 generated / ~8,500 accepted = ~$1,800
data_plan.gate: Accepted set covers >= 90% of strata with >= 5 conversations; Spanish share >= 35%; no stratum > 3% of data; dedup (MinHash on assistant turns) < 5% near-duplicates; hold out 300 conversations (disjoint scenario/tool/prompt families) as PhonePatterns-Eval BEFORE training

data_plan.what: Carve out (a) 1,024 conversations-turn windows (seq 4,096) as the NVFP4 calibration set, disjoint from eval, stratified across strata/languages; (b) 300-conversation held-out eval with reference responses written by Qwen3.8-Max + Claude Sonnet 5 and reconciled; (c) 200 human-labelled turns (team labels on the seven axes) for judge calibration.
data_plan.size: 1,024 calibration rows; 300 eval conversations (~3,600 turns); 200 human-labelled turns
data_plan.cost_estimate: Reference generation + double-judge on 3,600 turns: ~$150; human labelling: ~10 team-hours
data_plan.gate: Judge-human Spearman >= 0.7 per axis on the 200 labelled turns; otherwise revise rubrics before any model comparison

data_plan.what: Add 15% replay of our verified tau2-bench banking trajectories (re-rendered thinking-off) and 5% general Qwen chat/tool data to prevent forgetting; ensure all samples are rendered with the exact Qwen3.8 chat template with enable_thinking=false (empty think block) and tool results as tool-role messages.
data_plan.gate: Rendered token-for-token diff between training render and vLLM's runtime render of the same conversation is zero on 50 samples

training_plan: Base: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B bf16 (Apache-2.0), text-only; strip/ignore the vision tower if present in the checkpoint; keep the native MTP head untouched during SFT.

Method (P1): LoRA r=128, alpha=256, dropout 0.05, target ALL linear layers - attention q/k/v/o, GDN in_proj_qkv, in_proj_z, in_proj_a, in_proj_b, out_proj, MLP gate/up/down; NOT embeddings/lm_head/conv1d/norms. Rationale: a larger, all-layer delta is more likely to survive NVFP4 PTQ than our r=64 adapter; still fits one 96 GB GPU (bf16 weights ~54 GB + adapter + 8k-token activations with gradient checkpointing).

Hyperparameters: LR 1e-4 cosine, warmup 3%, 2 epochs over ~30M tokens, effective batch 32 sequences (micro-batch 1 x grad-accum 32), max seq 8,192 (long calls up to 16k in a second bucket), bf16, Liger/flash kernels, loss on assistant tokens only (both spoken content and tool_call JSON), user/tool/system masked; no packing across conversations.

Template alignment: render every sample with tokenizer.apply_chat_template(..., enable_thinking=False) so the assistant turn begins with the same empty think block vLLM will produce at inference (exact string for Qwen3.8 UNVERIFIED - diff against a vLLM render on 50 samples before training). Tool results as role=tool messages; tools passed in the tools argument, not hand-written into the system prompt.

Unattended Vast job: single script that pulls data from HF, trains, merges LoRA into bf16 (peft merge_and_unload), pushes merged bf16 + adapter to a private HF repo, then runs the tau3 banking dev eval (1 trial) and the PhonePatterns-Eval on the merged bf16 via vLLM 0.28.0 and pushes results JSON; checkpoint to HF every 500 steps so a preempted box loses < 1 h.

Gate after bf16 SFT: tau3-banking pass^1 >= base thinking-off (no regression), PhonePatterns-Eval composite >= base + 3 points with say/do >= 4.7/5 and escalation discipline >= base, Spanish split within 2 points of English. If fails: inspect judge rationales per stratum, regenerate weak strata, retrain (budget 3 iterations).

Quantization (P1): ModelOpt >= 0.46.0 hf_ptq on the merged bf16: MLP W4A4 NVFP4 g16 (quant_algo NVFP4, not W4A16_NVFP4); FP8 for attention q/k/v/o and GDN in_proj_qkv/z/out_proj; exclude lm_head, all *.conv1d, in_proj_a, in_proj_b, norms, embeddings, mtp.* (regex 'mtp*'); kv_cache_quant_algo none (bf16 KV) with an FP8-KV variant measured separately; calibration on the 1,024 in-domain rows. Alternative toolchain if ModelOpt's Qwen3.8 GDN handling fails: llm-compressor with the unsloth/RedHatAI compressed-tensors recipe (MLP layers 0-55 W4A4, attn/GDN FP8, ignore re:^mtp.*), noting RedHatAI's warning that this format only works in vLLM, not SGLang.

Quantization gate: NVFP4-merged within 0.5 pts composite of bf16-merged, within 1.0 pt on tau3 pass^1, MTP k=2 acceptance >= 0.75, KL(bf16||NVFP4) on 500 held-out turns <= 1.5x the base model's own KL under the same recipe; also check no degradation on the Spanish split (quantization can hit lower-resource tokens harder).

Fallback (P2) if the fine-tune does not survive PTQ: ModelOpt QLoRA - quantize.py --recipe nvfp4 (custom exclusions as above) --compress True on the base; train.py with qlora_nvfp4.yaml adapted (r=32-64, LR 2e-4, 1-2 epochs, seq 8k, DDP single GPU since FSDP2 export is unsupported); export.py; serve with --enable-lora. Pre-test: determinism/quality A/B at temperature 0 (vLLM issue #50059) before committing.
Fallback (P3): ship bf16 base + unmerged r=128 LoRA + MTP k=2 (already proven serving path) if neither P1 nor P2 passes gates within the timeline; NVFP4 becomes a follow-up.

Optional stage (only if S2 leaves >= 3,000 judge-rejected turns): one epoch of DPO/ORPO on (accepted, rejected) pairs for say/do and over-transfer, LR 5e-6, beta 0.1, after SFT and before merge; skip if SFT already hits say/do >= 4.8/5.
MTP head: measure acceptance with the adapter/merged weights; if < 0.75, consider a short MTP-head-only fine-tune on our data (tooling for Qwen3.8 MTP training is UNVERIFIED) or drop to k=1.
serving_plan: Engine: vLLM 0.28.0 (or newer) on one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 96 GB (sm_120); do not use older third-party benchmarks (0.19-0.24) as expectations - 0.28.0 shipped FlashInfer XQA on SM12x, B12X dense linear backends, fused post-conv MTP decode for Qwen3.5 GDN and GDN gates aligned with speculative tokens.

Reference launch (P1 NVFP4 merged model): vllm serve <org>/qwen3.8-27b-phone-nvfp4 --quantization modelopt (or compressed-tensors auto-detect) --mamba-cache-mode align --enable-prefix-caching --kv-cache-dtype auto --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 64 --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}' --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser <hermes or qwen3_coder - verify against Qwen3.8's chat template; the Qwen3.5 recipe says qwen3_coder, our earlier notes say native JSON/hermes: UNVERIFIED> --reasoning-parser qwen3 --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}' --override-generation-config '{"temperature":0}' --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92. Check the startup log for the NVFP4 linear backend; if it says Marlin/W4A16 fallback, force --linear-backend cutlass or flashinfer_cutlass; if the checkpoint is W4A16 you have the wrong recipe.

Prefix-cache verification (day 1 of serving work): send a 1.7k-token transcript twice, confirm vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total increases and turn-2 TTFT drops; repeat with 5, 10, 20-turn transcripts. If GDN prefix caching is a no-op (as for nemotron_h in issue #54504), file it and fall back to shorter max-model-len plus aggressive session pinning; this single check decides whether turn-N TTFT is flat or linear in call length.

KPI change: replace aggregate tok/s with P95 TTFAT (time to first answer or tool-call token, reasoning excluded, first turn of each call excluded) under N concurrent multi-turn sessions replayed from our synthetic traffic (short user turns ~30 tokens, long cached prefix 1.5-6k, ~60-120 token completions). Run a 'not-to-exceed' sweep N = 4, 8, 16, 24, 32, 48 and report the max N with P95 TTFAT < 600 ms; compute $/agent-minute = (Vast $/hr / 0.70 utilisation / 60) / N.

Ablations on the same replay: MTP k=0/1/2/3 (MTP-1 recommended for latency by the Qwen3.5 recipe, k=2 is our current; measure acceptance and P95 TTFAT, not just tok/s), bf16 KV vs FP8 KV, NVFP4 vs FP8 (Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 + merged delta is NOT viable per our earlier finding; compare against bf16+LoRA P3 instead), chunked-prefill max-num-batched-tokens 2048 vs 8192.

Cross-check with SGLang for one day: Pipecat's 101 ms P50 for Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 came from a pinned SGLang build without speculative decoding on a 5090; if SGLang beats vLLM 0.28 on P95 TTFAT at N=16 by > 20%, reconsider, noting compressed-tensors NVFP4 checkpoints (unsloth/RedHatAI recipe) do not run in SGLang.

Pipecat integration: reuse pipecat-examples/phonellm/server/bot.py with OpenAILLMService(base_url=<our vLLM>, model=<our id>, temperature=0, extra_body chat_template_kwargs enable_thinking=false); keep end_call as an async tool with cancel_on_interruption=False; run its naturalness.yaml/reservations.yaml pipecat-eval scenarios as a smoke test on every candidate.

Side-by-side baseline: run pipecat-ai/phonellm-alpha-1-nvfp4 (19.4 GB; validated only on vLLM 0.27.1/B200 - may need a separate venv) and the bf16 PhoneLLM on the same box against PhonePatterns-Eval and the latency sweep, so our comparison does not rely on Pipecat's unpublished harness.

Fallback serving (P2): vllm serve <nvfp4 base> --enable-lora --lora-modules phone=<adapter> --max-lora-rank 64 with the same flags; expect a decode-throughput penalty from LoRA kernels on top of FP4 GEMM; measure whether the net gain over P3 is more than memory. Fallback (P3): current bf16 base + unmerged LoRA + MTP k=2 launch, re-measured with the new KPI.

eval_plan.what: sierra-research/tau2-bench banking domain (and telecom as a transfer check), agent = our vLLM endpoint via LiteLLM openai/ prefix, thinking OFF, temperature 0; 1 trial on dev, 5 trials final; report pass^1 and pass^4 and transfer-to-human rate. Regression guard for tool correctness and the over-transfer failure.
eval_plan.baseline: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B thinking-off (bf16) on the same harness; secondary: our first r=64 adapter; nvidia/Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4 published tau2 Telecom 95.4 vs FP8 95.2 as the expected quantization delta scale

eval_plan.name: aiewf-eval (public Pipecat predecessor benchmark)
eval_plan.what: github.com/kwindla/aiewf-eval aiwf_medium_context: 30x30 scripted turns, tool_use_correct / instruction_following / kb_grounding judged by Claude against golden responses, TTFAT with 700 ms guideline. Run on our bf16-merged, NVFP4-merged and P2/P3 variants.
eval_plan.baseline: Pipecat's published rows: qwen3.8-27b thinking-off FP8 (Baseten) 98.2% / 649 ms P50; qwen3.8-27b NVFP4 (unsloth, SGLang, RTX 5090) 97.8% / 101 ms P50; nemotron-3-nano-30b 90.6%. Gate: our fine-tune must not drop below 97% (no regression on generic voice-agent skills)

eval_plan.name: PhonePatterns-Eval (ours, PhoneBench-shaped)
eval_plan.what: 300 held-out conversations (scenario/tool/prompt families disjoint from training; 40% Spanish; 25% >= 20 turns; both narration styles), each turn compared to a reconciled reference by a two-judge panel (Claude Sonnet 5 + GPT-5.4) on the seven PhoneBench axes, 1-5 scale, calibrated on 200 human-labelled turns (Spearman >= 0.7 per axis required). Programmatic pre-checks: say/do, do/say, re-ask, raw-data leakage, transfer rate. Reported per axis, per language, per turn-depth bucket, per taxonomy group.
eval_plan.baseline: Qwen3.8-27B base thinking-off (target: +3 composite, say/do >= 4.7/5), Qwen3.8-27B base thinking-on (to quantify what thinking-off costs), pipecat-ai/phonellm-alpha-1 (bf16 and NVFP4) run on our box, Claude Sonnet 5 via API as a frontier reference. Note absolute numbers are not comparable to PhoneBench's 72.3 - only relative ordering vs PhoneLLM on our set is claimable

eval_plan.name: Quantization delta and MTP acceptance
eval_plan.what: bf16-merged vs NVFP4-merged (bf16 KV and FP8 KV) on PhonePatterns-Eval and tau3 pass^1; KL divergence on 500 held-out assistant turns; MTP acceptance rate at k=1,2,3 from vLLM metrics on the replay traffic.
eval_plan.baseline: PhoneLLM's published deltas (-0.04 bf16 KV, -0.54 FP8 KV); community Qwen3.8-27B deltas (BFCL -0.96, MTP metric -0.97, GPQA -0.5 QAT); base-model KL under the identical recipe. Gate: <= 0.5 composite, acceptance >= 0.75

eval_plan.name: Latency / concurrency sweep
eval_plan.what: Multi-turn replay of synthetic phone traffic against vLLM on the RTX PRO 6000; P50/P95 TTFAT (first turn excluded), prefix-cache hit counter, max concurrency N at P95 < 600 ms; modeled $/agent-minute with stated Vast rate and 70% utilisation; ablate MTP k, KV dtype, precision, SGLang vs vLLM.
eval_plan.baseline: Our current bf16 + LoRA + MTP k=2 (215-323 tok/s at 8-16 streams, re-measured as TTFAT); PhoneLLM's modeled $0.0025/min at 44 concurrent processes on B200 (not directly comparable hardware); Pipecat's 101/318/592 ms P50/P95/max for Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 on a 5090

eval_plan.name: Pipecat smoke suite
eval_plan.what: pipecat-examples/phonellm pipecat-eval scenarios (naturalness.yaml, reservations.yaml) run end-to-end through OpenAILLMService against our endpoint, both narration styles via system prompt; plus 20 live scripted phone-style probes for barge-in and end_call-in-same-turn behaviour.
eval_plan.baseline: PhoneLLM on the same example bot; pass/fail per scenario

differentiators: Bilingual (English + Spanish) phone agent from an Apache-2.0 base; PhoneLLM is English-only under a Nemotron license.
Prompt-conditional narration: same model obeys 'acknowledge before slow tools' or 'never narrate' depending on the system prompt; PhoneLLM's reference prompt supports only the latter.

Explicit taxonomy of 50 phone-conversation patterns (too many results, not found + similar, widen search, read-back, hold/transfer etiquette, barge-in repair) with per-pattern programmatic checks - an open, stratified spec versus PhoneLLM's undisclosed 692 strata.
ASR-noise robustness trained in: synthetic mishearing in user turns with targeted repair and no-write-on-uncertain-value behaviour.
Long-call robustness split (>= 20 turns, >= 3 tool calls, mid-call slot changes) trained and reported separately, addressing the turn-4/5 collapse criticism of thinking-off models.
Calibrated escalation: trained to both transfer when warranted and refuse unnecessary transfers, with transfer rate reported per scenario class.

Reproducible eval harness (aiewf-eval fork + PhoneBench axes + taxonomy probes + Spanish + long-call splits) and a side-by-side PhoneLLM run on identical hardware - PhoneBench's harness is unpublished.

Serving on one RTX PRO 6000 with MTP k=2 and verified GDN prefix caching, reported as P95 TTFAT concurrency and modeled $/agent-minute using Pipecat's own convention; PhoneLLM/nemotron_h currently re-prefills every turn on GPU.
Published bf16-vs-NVFP4 delta per eval axis and per language, plus a documented selective-quantization recipe that keeps the MTP head serviceable.

risks.risk: Fine-tune delta does not survive NVFP4 PTQ (our LoRA delta was already below FP8 precision), so the quantized model regresses to base behaviour.
risks.mitigation: Larger delta (r=128 all-layer, 2 epochs, LR 1e-4); merge to bf16 before PTQ; in-domain calibration; hard KL/eval gates; P2 QLoRA-on-frozen-NVFP4 fallback where the adapter is trained against quantized activations; P3 bf16+LoRA release path kept alive.

risks.risk: ModelOpt / llm-compressor cannot quantize or export Qwen3.8's GDN module class cleanly (changelog shows 0.46.0 fixed GatedDeltaNet exclusions on Megatron-Core only; HF path UNVERIFIED).
risks.mitigation: Week-1 smoke test: PTQ the BASE model with our recipe, load in vLLM 0.28.0, confirm linear backend is native FP4 and MTP loads; if it fails, use the unsloth/RedHatAI compressed-tensors recipe or defer NVFP4 (P3).

risks.risk: Headroom is small: untuned Qwen3.8-27B already scores 70.0 on PhoneBench vs PhoneLLM 72.3; our gains may be within judge noise.
risks.mitigation: Report per-axis and per-split (Spanish, long-call, narration style) where the base is weakest; use 300-conversation eval with two judges and human calibration; treat style/say-do/escalation, bilinguality and latency as the claims, not gross accuracy.

risks.risk: Train/serve template mismatch again (thinking flag, empty think block, tool-call format/parser, tool-role rendering).
risks.mitigation: Zero-diff test between training render and vLLM runtime render on 50 samples; bake enable_thinking=false and temperature 0 into the vLLM launch; verify the correct --tool-call-parser against the Qwen3.8 template before generating data.

risks.risk: Synthetic data teaches teacher artefacts (Qwen3.8-Max verbosity, invented tool results) or judge-pleasing verbosity.
risks.mitigation: Real mock environments own the tool results (teacher never invents them); programmatic say/do and raw-data filters before judging; word-count caps; 50-conversation manual read per stage; judge family different from generator.

risks.risk: Over-transfer or under-transfer regressions (our first adapter over-transferred).
risks.mitigation: Balanced 10%/10% escalation-warranted vs in-scope-but-requested strata; transfer-rate metric on in-scope scenarios must stay ~0; tau3 banking transfer rate tracked every run.

risks.risk: vLLM prefix caching is a no-op for hybrid GDN layers (as for nemotron_h), making turn-N TTFT grow with call length and blowing the P95 budget.
risks.mitigation: Day-1 counter check; if broken, cap context, consider SGLang, and file/track the vLLM issue; report honestly.

risks.risk: MTP acceptance drops after fine-tuning (head trained on base activations), erasing the decode gain.
risks.mitigation: Measure acceptance on replay traffic; try k=1; optionally fine-tune the MTP head on our data (tooling UNVERIFIED).

risks.risk: Unattended Vast jobs fail (preemption, OOM at seq 16k, HF push errors) and burn budget.
risks.mitigation: Checkpoint to HF every 500 steps; smoke job on 100 samples first; 50% GPU budget buffer; separate long-sequence bucket with micro-batch 1.

risks.risk: Budget overrun on teacher tokens (turn-by-turn generation re-sends context every turn).
risks.mitigation: Lean tier (5,000 generated) first; use OpenRouter provider prompt caching where available; move simplest strata to glm-5.3-flash; keep generation logs to resume rather than regenerate.

risks.risk: Licensing of teacher outputs (Qwen3.8-Max, GLM-5.3 terms) or of PhoneLLM outputs for any use in training data.
risks.mitigation: Human review of provider terms before dataset release; do not use PhoneLLM outputs as training data unless cleared; student base is Apache-2.0.

risks.risk: PhoneLLM NVFP4 checkpoint validated only on vLLM 0.27.1/B200; may not run on our 0.28.0/sm_120 box for the side-by-side.
risks.mitigation: Run PhoneLLM bf16 (63 GB, fits) as the primary baseline; try NVFP4 in a separate venv; mark as best-effort.

refuted_or_unverified: REFUTED: 'RedHatAI has only the 2.4T MoE in NVFP4' - RedHatAI/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 exists (compressed-tensors, same recipe as unsloth; 'ONLY works in vLLM and NOT SGLang').

REFUTED: 'every PTQ recipe keeps the MTP head in BF16 and GDN projections in FP8/BF16' - gittensor removed the MTP head entirely; kristianpaul, gittensor, sakamakismile and QUASAR quantize GDN in_proj/out_proj to W4A4; dudeman2512 is W4A16 with no mtp ignore entries. vLLM's mtp.fc rescue applies only to modelopt_fp4 checkpoints, not compressed-tensors.

REFUTED (partially): 'an NVFP4 version of Qwen3.8-27B exists to build on' - no official Qwen or NVIDIA NVFP4; all are community checkpoints; nothing supports fine-tuning a pre-quantized checkpoint directly.
